solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Help to cover one end of lamp shade

indicators.note: an end of a word is one of its two outer letters, here the opening one
something that covers another wraps round it, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: to back someone is to help or support them
the first letter of lamp

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a hand putting a shade over one end of a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Black is a colour, and shade is a common word for a colour or tone.

clue.text: Something brought by the waiter containing dry, skinned fish

indicators.note: a skinned word has lost its outer layer, leaving only its inside letters
one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: a waiter brings the bill at the end of a meal
the middle letter of dry, its outer letters stripped

explanation.surface: A waiter serves a dish of dried, skinned fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish, close relative of the turbot, eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Artificial intelligence supported by loaded nerd who tried to take over the world?

definitions.text: who tried to take over the world?

indicators.note: loaded is slang for drunk, and a drunk word staggers into a new order
in a down entry, something supported sits above what holds it up

blocks.note: Alexa is Amazon's AI voice assistant
the letters of nerd rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy geek's AI plots world domination, like a villain in a techno-thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a description of the nerd, but it points to Alexander the Great.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great conquered most of the known world of his day, so he is one who tried to rule it all.

clue.text: Spades removed from trash and extension emptied to make room

indicators.note: taking something away from a word leaves it a letter shorter
an emptied word has had its insides taken out, keeping only its first and last letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in cards; this letter is taken out
kitsch is tasteless, trashy art
the first and last letters of extension

explanation.surface: Clearing out rubbish and an emptied extension to free up space in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes out of the middle of KITSCH, leaving KITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is a room in a house where food is cooked.

clue.text: Children jump out in front

indicators.note: placing a word in front puts it before the other piece

blocks.note: off and out both mean away or departed
to spring is to jump

explanation.surface: Kids leaping out ahead of the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children or descendants.

clue.text: Happen to finally see copper on robber's tail

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
a word's tail is its final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of to
the letter C is pronounced like the word see
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the last letter of robber

explanation.surface: A policeman finally catches up with a fleeing robber.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer chasing the robber, but here it is the metal. The homophone of see has no separate signal: C is simply the letter that sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen or take place.

clue.text: Something inside leaves through the centre of extortionately flaccid bum

indicators.note: the centre of a long word is its middle pair of letters
one piece runs through the middle of another, ending up inside it
bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are in a broken order

blocks.note: the two central letters of this fourteen-letter word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rude remark about someone's saggy backside costing a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The IO goes into FLACCID and the whole lot is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Folic acid, a B vitamin, takes its name from the Latin for leaf because it was first found in spinach and other leafy greens.

clue.text: Go over 70, say, in alley

blocks.note: to pass is to go over or across
seventy is an example of an age; say marks it as one instance

explanation.surface: A speeding driver goes over seventy in a narrow lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 70 reads as a speed limit, but it stands for a person's age.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a narrow way between buildings, much as an alley is.

clue.text: Some deride a scientist's theories

indicators.note: only some of the following words' letters are used, a run lying inside them

blocks.note: the run starts near the end of deride and finishes at the start of scientist's

explanation.surface: Some people mock a scientist's theories.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas and theories are both notions or proposed explanations.

clue.text: Those attending car accident turn up uninvited

blocks.note: a gate is the number of people attending a sports event
a crash is a collision between vehicles

explanation.surface: Spectators drawn to a road accident arrive without being asked.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to attend a party or event without an invitation.

clue.text: Weirdly, Neil and Di act exactly the same

indicators.note: something done weirdly is done strangely, so the letters fall in an odd order

blocks.note: the letters of the two names and the verb, with and as a joining word

explanation.surface: A couple, Neil and Di, oddly behave in exactly the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: The and simply joins the two names and is not part of the letters used.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things match in every detail, with no difference at all.

clue.text: Virtuous woman eating small dessert

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: ST, saint, the abbreviation for a holy person
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A well-behaved woman tucks into a little pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet is the British word for the dessert course of a meal.

clue.text: Hide article penned by purveyor of nonsense

indicators.note: something penned is shut in a pen, enclosed by the other piece

blocks.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat
the definite article

explanation.surface: A writer of nonsense pens a piece and tucks it away.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide looks like a verb, but it is the noun for an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal hide, so the two name the same material.

clue.text: How might one describe Lord of the Flies? 'Schoolchildren in charge'?

definitions.text: How might one describe Lord of the Flies?

blocks.note: a class is a group of schoolchildren
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Lord of the Flies is summed up as a story of schoolboys running things themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: William Golding's novel shows stranded schoolboys ruling themselves, so the wordplay doubles as a plot summary.
explanation.definitionFit: Golding's novel is a celebrated, enduring work of literature, which is what a classic is.

clue.text: One gets carried away sculpting sand close to dune

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, its final letter
sculpting shapes material into a new form, so the letters are remodelled

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of dune

explanation.surface: Someone becomes absorbed in building sandcastles by a dune.
explanation.walkthrough: Carried away suggests enthusiasm; it means literally carried, as in a sedan chair borne on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles by bearers, so whoever rides in one is carried.

clue.text: Order given to the driver?

blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction to a chauffeur or cabbie
setter's reading: what a designated driver asks for at the bar, something without alcohol

explanation.walkthrough: Order sounds like a command, but it is a drinks order, and the driver cannot drink alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft drink is non-alcoholic, the usual choice for someone who has to drive home.

clue.text: York's centre-half and left-winger alongside an assortment of star players

indicators.note: the central half of a four-letter word is its middle two letters
an assortment is a mixed collection, so the letters come mixed up

blocks.note: the two middle letters of York
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, a famous figure of the political left
the letters of star rearranged

explanation.surface: A football report on York City's defender and winger lining up with a team of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre-half and left-winger are football positions, but here one picks letters and the other is a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of musicians who play together.

clue.text: Undressed lovers sketch figures in red

indicators.note: an undressed word has its outer covering stripped, losing its first and last letters

blocks.note: lovers without its first and last letters
a draft is a rough sketch

explanation.surface: Naked lovers drawn by an artist working in red.
explanation.walkthrough: In red means in debt on a bank statement, not the colour of the drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft takes a bank balance below zero, and such figures are said to be in the red.

clue.text: Liqueur left amongst a jumble of receipts

indicators.note: something amongst others is placed in their midst
a jumble is a disordered heap, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bottle of liqueur left in a pile of shop receipts.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is a clear orange-flavoured liqueur, as used in a margarita.

clue.text: Police officers drugged American agent to impose a way of thinking

indicators.note: a drugged person has a drug put inside them

blocks.note: the force is the police
a fed is an FBI agent in US slang
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Police dope a US agent to brainwash him, like a spy thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: Drugged does double duty here: it signals the insertion and supplies the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To force-feed ideas is to press them on someone against their will, like feeding by force.

clue.text: Bring forth fruit thief smuggling cherimoya peel in books

indicators.note: the peel of a fruit is its outside, here the outer letters of the word
a smuggler carries something hidden inside
one piece placed in another

blocks.note: Eve took the forbidden fruit in Genesis
OT, the Old Testament, a set of books
the first and last letters of cherimoya

explanation.surface: A shoplifter sneaks an exotic fruit out tucked into books.
explanation.walkthrough: CA goes into OT, and that goes into EVE. A cherimoya is a South American custard apple.
explanation.definitionFit: To evocate is an old form of evoke, meaning to call up or bring forth.

clue.text: Carefully consider plan out loud

indicators.note: said out loud, a word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a way is a plan or method

explanation.surface: Someone is told to think a scheme over carefully and talk it through.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh options is to consider them carefully, balancing one against another.

clue.text: Cover of Whigfield's number one by Eminem?

indicators.note: number one means the first, so the first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Whigfield
Eminem is a famous rapper, an example, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Eminem covers Whigfield's chart-topper, a pop-music odd couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Whigfield had a 1994 number one with Saturday Night, and a cover version sounds like the point; cover is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is an outer covering, such as the paper round a sweet.

clue.text: Did a second bridge player put in card?

indicators.note: pieces put in are placed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second
North is one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A question about whether another bridge player played a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is a playing card of the suit marked with red lozenges.

clue.text: A political party containing 500 in total

indicators.note: the party holds the number inside itself

blocks.note: taken as written
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A party has 500 members altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: To add up is to total figures by summing them.

clue.text: Buy wife pale yellow trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser something is to pocket it, holding it inside

blocks.note: sallow skin has a sickly pale yellow tinge
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A shopping instruction to purchase pale yellow trousers for one's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Buy is the informal sense of believe, as in I don't buy that story; trousers is a verb, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is to accept it as true, just as one may buy it.

clue.text: Barman that is beginning to serve at opening

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of serve
taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A pub barman is about to start serving as the doors open.
explanation.walkthrough: Barman means a composer, a man who writes bars of music. S and AT come at the opening, ahead of IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, and a composer writes music in bars.

clue.text: They move first and knock into you and me

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, ending up inside it

blocks.note: we is you and me together
to knock is to hit

explanation.surface: Someone moves first and bumps into the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the side playing White always makes the opening move.

clue.text: Country hotel's nearby

blocks.note: first meaning: the South Asian nation
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the code word right after Hotel

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a travel ad for a country hotel; Hotel is the code word for H, and the next letter's code word follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: India is both a country and the radio code word for I, which follows Hotel for H in the alphabet.

clue.text: Distribute pittas in a set of small dishes

indicators.note: distributing things spreads them about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Handing round pitta bread on a selection of small plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters, an assortment of small dishes served before the main meal.

clue.text: Neckwear of UKIP leader leaving a football match?

indicators.note: when the leader leaves, the first letter drops away

blocks.note: the UK Independence Party
per means for each, as in ten pounds a head
a tie is a knockout football match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A UKIP leader walks out of a football game, wearing loud neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The U of UKIP is dropped. The surface also hints at Kippers, the nickname for UKIP supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper tie is a very wide, brightly patterned necktie fashionable in the 1970s.

clue.text: Look around vacant caravanette next to playground

indicators.note: a vacant word has nothing inside, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: the rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field
the first and last letters of caravanette

explanation.surface: Checking out an empty camper van parked by a play area.
explanation.walkthrough: A caravanette is a British word for a small camper van.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is a scouting look around a place.
